newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Heavy security around U.S. embassy in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Heavy security around U.S. embassy in Albania.

text.p: Albanian police surrounded the U.S. embassy for a second day on Wednesday, closing nearby cafes and driving off youths who appeared set on storming the compound.
Dozens of police took up positions with assault rifles and bullet-proof jackets around the sprawling compound in central Tirana. An armoured personnel carrier was parked permanently outside.
Police drove off dozens of youths seated at nearby cafes and stopped others from approaching the embassy. Police said they detained a number of youths and whisked them off to jail.
On Tuesday, police fired shots in the air to disperse about 100 youths who were trying to reach the compound.
Police said rumours had swept Tirana that the U.S. embassy would open its gates to people wanting to flee Albania, swept by unrest for three months and suffering a revolt in the south.
"Someone starts these rumours and then it's difficult to change their minds," said the owner of the nearby Endri cafe.
Witnesses said police cleared out about 20 customers from Endri cafe, including a couple with two children and two large bags, and then closed it for the day.
Tirana police chief Pashk Dusha told Albanian television: "Yesterday and today some Albanians gathered around the territory of the U.S. embassy.
"Tirana police with all its means, equipment and forces immediately took the necessary steps to resolve the situation and to create normal conditions of calm and security."

U.S. marines at the compound have beefed up security in recent days. They put additional barbed-wire on a high security fence and set up manned sandbag positions on the rooftop of the Italian-style villa.

An embassy statement was read on television on Wednesday, denying rumours that the compound would be opened to the public and stressing that anyone going to the U.S. required a visa. It said no visas were being issued at the moment.
Thousands of Albanians stormed Western embassies in 1990, climbing into the Italian, German and Turkish compounds among others.
The United States took over the Italian embassy compound when it reestablished relations with Albania in 1991 after a Stalinist regime which had ruled for 45 years collapsed.
